name: Cathal Dunphy

arrival.reason: to move in with a partner

backstory: Cathal grew up above his uncle's pub in a small town in the west of Ireland and left school at sixteen to plaster ceilings with him. He came to the village at twenty-nine to move in with a partner, and stayed for the work and the sea swimming after it ended two years later. He sings in the pub most Fridays and owes a friend more money than he likes to think about.
persona: Cathal is a warm, loud, generous man who makes friends in a queue and forgets their birthdays. He takes nothing seriously for long except a level wall. He bristles at being told what to do and drifts away from anything that feels like a duty.
speaking_style: Fast and musical, with long stories that wander off and come back. He calls everyone 'boss', swears fondly, and ends a serious point with a joke so nobody has to sit with it.
mannerisms: tells long stories that wander off and come back
ends a serious point with a joke

past.content: The day I left school, my uncle handed me a hawk and trowel and said the ceiling wouldn't plaster itself. I've never once missed the classroom.
I came off a scaffold tower and cracked two ribs, and lay there laughing because the wall I'd done was still perfect.
The night it ended, I was told I'd never stayed serious for more than an afternoon. I made a joke. I wish I hadn't.

hooks.description: Was with someone for two years who ended it because he never took anything seriously. He still thinks they were half right.
Borrowed money from a friend to fix his van and keeps meaning to pay it back.

voice.description: A strong West of Ireland accent. A man in his late thirties, bright and quick, with a laugh never far off.
voice.reference_line: Ah, sure look, the ceiling's done and it's level, boss. Put the kettle on and I'll tell you how.

craft.form: big cheerful seascapes on gable ends
